questions.solution_html:

  • mainly through elections and social movements

questions.question: Interpret the role of land and forest rights in Adivasi movements. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Land and forest rights form the core of Adivasi (indigenous) movements representing a
  • struggle for physical survival, cultural identity, self-governance, and resistance against
  • historical and modern displacement----Adivasi movements for identity autonomy and social
  • justice—land and forest are essential for Adivasis livelihood---The Forest Rights Act (FRA),
  • 2006----Gram Sabha as a Weapon of Resistance---Constitutional Protections.

questions.question: Explain how agrarian movements are connected with land and livelihood. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Agrarian movements are collective struggles by rural populations—including small peasants,
  • tenants, landless agricultural laborers, and rich farmers—to challenge exploitative structures
  • and secure control over land and livelihood. Land is not merely an economic asset; it is the
  • foundation of social identity, survival, and autonomy in rural societies.

questions.question: Explain the basic assumptions of the Liberal approach to Political Sociology. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The liberal approach to political sociology centres on the individual as the primary actor in
  • society, viewing political institutions and social structures as mechanisms meant to protect
  • personal freedom, foster cooperation, and limit state power---political pluralism—political
  • participation—rule of law.

questions.question: Explain the basic assumptions of the Marxist approach. / [CO1] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• The Marxist approach in political sociology views politics, the state, and power not as
  • independent or neutral spheres, but as direct reflections of a society's underlying economic
  • and material conditions---state as an instrument of class domination—historical
  • materialism—capitalist exploitation.
  • Part-C

questions.question: Trace the historical evolution of Political Sociology as a discipline in India. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Political sociology in India emerged as a distinct interdisciplinary field following
  • independence in 1947--Pre-Independence Foundations (Colonial Era to 1947)--- Colonial
  • Ethnography and Administration---Institutional Emergence---National Awakening and
  • Reform--Post-Independence Institutionalization (1950s–1960s)-- Bridging Political Science
  • and Sociology---Foundational Professional Bodies-- The formation of the Indian Sociological
  • Society in 1951--The Dominant Caste and Village Power--M.N. Srinivas introduced crucial
  • frameworks such as thedominant caste and vote bank---The Golden Era of Politicization
  • Studies (1970s–1980s)-- The Politicization of Caste----Tradition and Modernity Debates---
  • Agrarian Class and Structural Analyses--Democratic Upsurges and Identity Politics (1990s–
  • 2000s)--- The First and Second Democratic Upsurges--Decoupling Ritual and Political
  • Power--Political Society vs. Civil Society--Contemporary Trends --Aspirational Politics and
  • Beneficiary Bases----Interdisciplinary Expansion.

questions.question: Evaluate the relationship between digital platforms, public opinion and political mobilisation. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Digital platforms transform public opinion and political mobilisation by bypassing traditional
  • media gatekeepers, enabling direct leader-to-citizen communication, and lowering the barriers
  • to collective action, while simultaneously accelerating polarization, echo chambers, and the
  • spread of misinformation-----Digital connectivity empowers ordinary citizens and
  • marginalized communities to organize social movements, protest campaigns, and civic
  • activities online that rapidly translate into offline--Direct Leader-Public Connectivity--Hybrid
  • Campaigning--Reactive Public Discourse etc..

questions.question: Define political economy and critically examine its scope and limitations in understanding globalization. / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Political economy is an interdisciplinary social science that studies how political institutions,
  • power dynamics, and legal frameworks mutually influence economic systems, market
  • behaviour, and the distribution of wealth and resources---scope in globalisation--State-Market
  • Relations--Power Asymmetries and Class Dynamics--Institutional and Regulatory
  • Frameworks--Policy Choices and Resistance--Crisis Management—Limitations--State-
  • Centric Bias—Reductionism-Difficulty in Quantifying Cultural and Psychological Factors---
  • Pace and Complexity of Technological Disruption---Predictive Weakness—insufficient
  • attention to culture—identity gender and environmental factors.
